subject.title: Cron run drops a produced deliverable when an ancillary backgrounded tool exits non-zero

question: Should isolated cron runs with final assistant output after a non-terminal background/exec failure persist as `ok`, a new degraded/warning outcome, or `error`, and what typed evidence qualifies the failure as recovered?
rationale: Current source shows the bug family is real, but changing the status contract affects delivery, failure alerts, retries, backoff, monitoring, and operator expectations; automation cannot safely choose that product boundary.

options.title: Add Degraded Outcome
options.body: Introduce typed exec/process-started failure-phase evidence and a first-class degraded/warning cron outcome that can deliver the result while preserving operator-visible diagnostics.

options.title: Narrow Existing Recovery
options.body: Keep the current ok/error states and recover only explicit non-terminal warning metadata or maintainer-approved recovery markers, leaving ambiguous process-ran failures fatal.

options.title: Preserve Fail-Closed Contract
options.body: Keep ancillary non-zero process exits fatal for cron delivery and document failure-destination or watchdog workarounds instead of changing status semantics.

recommendation.title: Add Degraded Outcome
recommendation.body: Introduce typed exec/process-started failure-phase evidence and a first-class degraded/warning cron outcome that can deliver the result while preserving operator-visible diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: The related maintainer discussion already narrowed the remaining implementation to typed exec phase evidence plus degraded cron outcome semantics.
